title: DEEP/ULTRA brief [n] citations point at the wrong documents: markers minted against one source numbering survive into a brief published under another
repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Deep research on Blue Star (BLUESTARCO): room-AC demand, margin trend, and is the valuation justified versus Voltas and Lloyd? Cite sources.' --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini --autonomy auto, options.research_depth=deep, on :52218 -> published brief cites 'Closing Price ₹1,525.0 [6]', 'Market Capitalization [7]', 'P/E 61.67 [7]', margins/oil prices/MedTech divestment all [7] (15 markers). Rail source [7] = nsearchives BLUESTARCO_06082026143619_BSLBMchangeindirectors06082026.pdf, fetched: 'Sub.: Change in Directorate … approved appointment of Mr Nikhilesh Panchal … as an Additional Director'. [6] = the Q1FY27 shareholder communication PDF. The figures actually came from [11] vysted://price and [12] vysted://fundamentals.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r4-deep-bluestar-4omini.jsonl (publish_brief input), replay-r4-deep-bluestar-4omini.json (BriefPanel renders chips 6/7 against a 13-row rail), EVIDENCE.md 'Finding 1'; sidecar/services/research/deep.py:356-373 (all_sources: ranked web/filings first, structured last), sidecar/services/research/iter.py:127-129 (_numbered_sources renumbers every round), iter.py:223-260 (synthesis copies the working report's markers); corroborated by agent B's runs in the same dir: 13-ultra-hal-4omini.jsonl (ULTRA, gpt-4o-mini) cites 'Closing Price ₹4,800.0 [1]' -> [1] = a BSE 'Change in Directorate' PDF, 'Market Capitalization ₹3.21 trillion [2]' / 'P/E 34.42 [2]' -> [2] = nsearchives HAL_10092026174050_changeindirector_signed.pdf, margins '[3]' -> [3] = HAL_08092026150304_AON_ALH_08092026.pdf (each angle distilled against a 3-source list where [1..3] were vysted://price|fundamentals|news; the merged brief has 5 filings ahead of them); control case 12-deep-bdl-4omini.jsonl: source count stayed 8 every round and its [6]/[7] markers DO land on vysted://price/fundamentals
notes: Every-figure-traceable is the product's research promise; here every figure's chip opens an unrelated filing. Mechanism: round 1 distilled with 8 sources (step 'distilled … 8 source(s)'), so price/fundamentals were [6]/[7]; rounds 2-5 inserted 5 more filings AHEAD of the structured legs (13 sources) but the evolving report keeps '[7]' text and the final synthesis reuses it. The citation check only strips out-of-range markers ('stripped 0 out-of-range marker(s)'), so in-range stale markers ship. Figures themselves verified correct on screener.in (price 1,525, mcap ₹31,356 cr). Reproduced on 2 of 2 multi-list runs (DEEP Blue Star, ULTRA HAL) and absent on the one run whose source list never changed (BDL, 8 sources every round) — the control that pins the mechanism. Smallest fix: give each source a stable id at first sight (append-only numbering, never re-rank after a marker was minted), or rewrite report markers by URL when the list is re-ranked; add a citecheck that a marker's source can actually support the sentence's figure (structured legs for price/ratios).

title: On the local lane DEEP/ULTRA synthesis times out at 60 s and silently ships the structured floor, blamed on 'thin web coverage' while 13+ web sources were captured
repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Do a deep research brief on CG Power and Industrial Solutions — order book, margins, and whether the valuation is justified versus peers.' --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --autonomy auto, research_depth=deep -> step 'synthesize | wrote brief from evolving report | 60014 ms', 'audit skipped (-60s wall remaining < 15s)'; published markdown = '_Web coverage for this name is thin; this brief is built from exchange data and filings gathered this run._' + a filings list + 'change % -1.527472527472525' + 'market cap 1411777036288.0' — while the same brief carries 13 http web sources + 5 filings. Agent B's independent BDL run (11-deep-bdl-llama): synthesize 60007 ms, identical floor. ULTRA (r3-ultra-kaynes): all three angle syntheses 60001-60012 ms.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r2-deep-cgpower.jsonl + .stdout.txt, 11-deep-bdl-llama.jsonl, r3-ultra-kaynes.stdout.txt, replay-r2-deep-cgpower.json (panel header 'DEEP · 21 sources · web + structured data', no note, execution.degraded_reason null); sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:69 (_LLM_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECS = 60.0), :322-325; sidecar/services/research/iter.py:261-272 (empty synthesis -> floor); sidecar/services/research/deep.py:523-556 (floor copy + raw f'{label} {val}' formatting at :459-505)
notes: The keyless/local lane is the product's zero-setup default, and 2/2 DEEP + 1/1 ULTRA runs on it ended in the floor (contended machine — a second agent drove the same ollama — but an 8B model reading a ~16k-token report+sources prompt on an M1 routinely exceeds 60 s). The user asked about order book, margins and peer valuation and got an unanswered data dump labelled DEEP, with the failure misattributed to web coverage (the opposite of the truth) and no degraded_reason/note, so nothing in the panel says the analysis step died. Smallest fix: scale the per-call cap for local providers (or stream synthesis with a progress deadline), and when the floor fires because synthesis returned empty, set execution.degraded_reason='synthesis_timeout' + a note naming it; the floor copy must only claim thin coverage when web_sources is actually empty; format floor numbers (%, crore/INR) instead of raw floats.

title: ULTRA cross-check mangles every decimal figure ('40.5%'->'5%', '67.13953'->'13953') and its step reports 'verified 5 numeric claim(s), 0 disagreement(s)' over five UNVERIFIED rows
repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Research Kaynes Technology in depth: …' --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --autonomy auto, research_depth=ultra -> brief body figures: revenue growth +40.5%, earnings growth -0.4%, below 52w high 55.16%, P/E 67.13953, mcap 232253702144.0; the brief's '## Cross-check' section renders 'UNVERIFIED — 5%', 'UNVERIFIED — 4%', 'UNVERIFIED — 16%', 'UNVERIFIED — 13953', 'UNVERIFIED — 232253702144'; the step trace says 'cross-check: verified 5 numeric claim(s), 0 disagreement(s)'.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r3-ultra-kaynes.jsonl + .stdout.txt, replay-r3-ultra-kaynes.json (BriefPanel renders the mangled cross-check list); sidecar/services/research/verify.py:137-158 (_extract_claims feeds the claim list through _split_subquestions), sidecar/services/research/deep.py:179-202 (strips any leading '<digits>.' / '<digits>)' as an ordered-list marker, and '-' as a bullet), verify.py:414-418 (step label counts checks, not verified ones); corroborated with a paid model by agent B's 13-ultra-hal-4omini.jsonl: body 'P/E 34.42', 'Gross Margin 51.70%', 'Revenue Growth 14.4%' -> cross-check rows 'UNVERIFIED — 42', 'UNVERIFIED — 70%', 'UNVERIFIED — 4% year-over-year'; step again 'cross-check: verified 5 numeric claim(s), 0 disagreement(s)'
notes: Reproduced on 2 of 2 ULTRA runs (llama3.1:8b Kaynes, gpt-4o-mini HAL). The ULTRA tier's marquee promise is 'every top figure re-checked'; in practice any claim line that STARTS with its figure loses the integer part ('40.5% revenue growth' -> '5% revenue growth', '-0.4%' -> '4%'), so the verifier searches for and prints the wrong number, and the trace tells the user 5 claims were verified with no disagreement. The mangled figures are rendered in the brief body. Related but distinct from COD-research-depth-iter-deep-1 (AGREE printed over UNVERIFIED). Smallest fix: a claim-specific splitter that only strips '<digits>. ' followed by whitespace+non-digit (never '<digits>.<digits>'), and a step label that states verified/unverified/disagree counts separately.

title: Managed SearXNG reports 'ready' while every upstream engine is CAPTCHA-blocked: Settings says research routes through it, every brief says 'set up Unlimited local research'
subsystem: searxng_manager health probe + web_search fallback + BriefPanel keyless nudge + SettingsPanel search section
repro: GET :52218/search/searxng/status -> {state: ready, detail: 'SearXNG serving JSON search at http://127.0.0.1:8888'}; the same container, GET 127.0.0.1:8888/search?q=KPIT+Technologies+share&format=json -> results: 0, unresponsive_engines: [[brave,'too many requests'],[duckduckgo,'CAPTCHA'],[startpage,'Suspended: CAPTCHA']]; the briefs whose web leg ran published backend 'keyless-fallback' (10-normal-kpit, r2-deep-cgpower), and the DEEP/ULTRA runs r3/r4 captured ZERO http web sources.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/http-log.jsonl, EVIDENCE.md 'Finding 3', replay-10-normal-kpit.json (renders 'Limited keyless search — set up Unlimited local research for full capability.'); sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:161-179 (_probe_health: any results LIST, empty included, is healthy; unresponsive_engines ignored), sidecar/services/agent_tools/web_search.py:148-166 (every empty SearXNG answer silently re-served by the keyless floor); src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:908-913 ('Running … research searches route through it automatically'); src/modules/research/BriefPanel.tsx:348-377 (nudge + link to Settings)
notes: Two surfaces contradict each other and both are wrong about the cause: Settings is green, the brief sends the user to set up something already running, and the real cause (the container's upstream engines are blocked, so 'Unlimited' is actually serving zero results) appears nowhere. The user cannot act on it. Smallest fix: have the health probe read unresponsive_engines (all engines unresponsive or a run of empty answers -> a 'degraded' state with the engine reasons), surface that state in Settings, and key the brief nudge copy on it ('SearXNG is running but its search engines are blocked — …') instead of 'set up'.

title: The 'kept previous brief' divergence notice (live) is not recognised by the chat's notice regex and is buried as a step row in the collapsed trace
repro: ULTRA run under autonomy=auto with the frontend's ack for the autobrief posted as status=kept_previous (harness/turn.py --ack kept_previous) -> end-of-stream research_step {step_kind: engine, detail: 'The panel kept the brief already on screen — this publish did not replace it; do not claim the new one rendered.'}. DIVERGENCE_RE = /did not confirm the publish|kept the previous, richer brief/i does not match it, so ChatSidebar routes it to appendResearchStep (a trace row under the collapsed 'Worked for … · N steps' line) instead of the transcript notice chip — while the model's prose above it already said 'The research brief provides a comprehensive overview'.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r3-ultra-kaynes.stdout.txt (last research_step), replay-r3-ultra-kaynes.json engineNotices; sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1029-1035 (kept_previous copy); src/modules/chat/message-notices.ts:57-61 (regex); src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:981-990 (non-matching engine steps go to the trace), :295-352 (trace collapsed by default after the run)
notes: Live confirmation of COD-error-layer-1 (code-read found 2 of 3 notices unmatched). The one moment the runtime tells the truth that the panel did NOT change is hidden behind a collapsed disclosure, and the visible transcript keeps the model's claim that the brief landed. Smallest fix: key notices on a structured field (e.g. a dedicated step_kind 'notice' or code) instead of prose regex, or share the copy constants between runtime and frontend.

title: ULTRA brief ships an invented 'Merged Sources'/'References' list and literal '[n] 1' markers that the citation check never inspects
subsystem: research heavy-panel single-call angle merge + citecheck
repro: r3-ultra-kaynes published markdown: 'Earnings growth: -0.4% (… [n] 1)', a '**Merged Sources**' list of 7 items and a 'References:' list '[n] 1. Quarterly income statements …' … '[n] 7. Exchange filings regarding AGM proceedings ([n] 9)' — while the brief's real sources are 3 (vysted://price, vysted://fundamentals, vysted://news; 0 web). BriefPanel renders both invented lists verbatim above a 'Sources (3)' rail.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r3-ultra-kaynes.jsonl (publish_brief markdown + sources), replay-r3-ultra-kaynes.json renderedText; step 'citation check: stripped 0 out-of-range marker(s)'; src/lib/brief-ingest.ts:392 (CITE_MARKER_RE only knows '[digits]', so '[n] 1' passes through as text); agent B's 13-ultra-hal-4omini.jsonl (gpt-4o-mini) also ends with a model-authored '### Sources' list and states 'recent ones for integrated services in complex deepwater developments off Cyprus [3]' for HAL, cited to an AON_ALH filing
notes: A weak synthesis model fabricated a bibliography; the product labels the result ULTRA ('HEAVY · deepest') with no note that it has zero web sources and a fake reference list, so a reader sees 7-9 'sources' that do not exist. The citation check validates only numeric [n] ranges. Smallest fix: strip model-authored reference/source sections from the synthesis (the rail is the only bibliography), reject '[n]'-literal markers, and when an ULTRA run ends with < min_web_domains web sources say so in brief.note / degraded_reason.

title: A free-model shared-pool 429 is told to the user as 'OpenRouter is rate-limiting your account — wait a moment' (3 of 3 free models failed in a row)
repro: vy.py invoke copilot '<research prompt>' --provider openrouter --model google/gemma-4-31b-it:free (then qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free) -> error frame message 'OpenRouter is rate-limiting your account — try again in a minute.', action 'Wait a moment, then try again.'; the provider's own detail says 'limit_source': 'upstream_provider_shared_pool', remedy 'route to another provider'. The raw detail (shown behind 'Details') also carries the OpenRouter 'user_id'.
notes: For a :free slug the pool is shared by every OpenRouter user, so 'wait a minute' is often false and 'your account' is wrong; the working remedy is to pick another model. Distinct from COD-error-layer-5 (OpenAI no-credit 429). Smallest fix: branch on limit_source/':free' to say 'this free model is saturated upstream — pick another model' with a model-switch action; scrub user_id from detail.

title: On the Ollama lane every tool call carries tool_call_id '' so no host action (incl. a model-issued publish_brief) can ever be acked: AUTO read-back is permanently 'unconfirmed'
subsystem: llm/ollama adapter ids + host-action ack read-back (action_ledger) + frontend ackHostAction
repro: Every llama3.1:8b tool_use this session streamed tool_call_id '' (r2-deep-cgpower 12 events, r3-ultra-kaynes 28, r5 2, conv1-t1 2, conv1-t2 1). The frontend's ack for such a call is skipped (`if (!toolCallId) return`), and even a direct POST /agents/actions/ack {tool_call_id:'', status:'applied'} -> HTTP 422 'String should have at least 1 character'. So under autonomy=auto the runtime's grace-window read-back always finds no entry.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/http-log.jsonl (the 422), r3-ultra-kaynes.jsonl / r2-deep-cgpower.jsonl (tool_call_id ''); sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:212 (`tool_call_id=_attr(tool_call, 'id', '') or ''`); sidecar/routers/agents.py:49 (min_length=1); src/lib/host-actions.ts:1452-1459 (early return on empty id); sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1103-1112 + :1614-1626 (no ack -> 'dispatched_unconfirmed'), :1006-1030 (model-issued publish_brief with no ack -> 'The brief panel did not confirm the publish' notice)
notes: Live consequence on the zero-setup default lane: every AUTO host action the model takes (watchlist add, note, layout, publish) is reported back to it as 'dispatched, not yet confirmed — verify before claiming success', and a publish_brief the model issues itself always ends the turn with a 'did not confirm the publish' chip even when the brief rendered — the honesty machinery can only ever say 'unconfirmed' here. Two research calls in one turn also share the synthetic id '__autobrief'. Code-read counterpart: COD-llm-adapters-2-5 (non-unique Ollama ids); this adds the live 422 and the user-visible consequence. Smallest fix: mint a uuid in the Ollama adapter when the SDK returns no id (the runtime already carries ids through the tool-result turn).

title: DEEP brief states a rival company's order-book win and renewable-energy projects as Bharat Dynamics' own, cited to a generic 'News for BDL' source — the structured news leg has no relevance gate
subsystem: research/deep._record_structured (news dim) vs research/fast._news_value (row_relevant gate) + services/news_provider region-wide feed blending
repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Bharat Dynamics — order book, margins and valuation' --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini --autonomy auto, research_depth=deep, symbol=BDL, on :52218 -> published brief's 'Order Book and Future Growth' section states 'BDL has secured domestic and international contracts exceeding ₹985 crore, which are anticipated to bolster its growth [8]' and 'BDL is actively enhancing its portfolio with renewable energy projects, including a 534.3 MWp solar project … and a 616 MWh energy storage capacity project …'. Source [8] = 'News for BDL' (generic vysted://news/BDL structured source, not a specific article). The underlying news tool call (21-news-tool-BDL.json) returns this as item id 1e4af0a955903e90: title 'Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy shares rally 8% after securing Rs 985 crore domestic and global orders' (ET, symbols: []) — an entirely different, unrelated listed company (a solar EPC firm, not a defence PSU). BDL itself has no such order or renewable-energy project.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/12-deep-bdl-4omini.jsonl (publish_brief input: markdown 'Order Book and Future Growth' section, sources[7] = 'News for BDL'), 21-news-tool-BDL.json (news tool result: item 1e4af0a955903e90, symbols: [], title/summary naming Sterling and Wilson, not BDL); sidecar/services/research/deep.py:376-393 (_record_structured folds the whole 'news' tool result into ONE generic ResearchSource per symbol, no per-item check), :715-716 (dim='news', tool='news', args={'symbols':[symbol]}), :1140-1148 (structured_pairs folded via _record_structured with no relevance filter); contrast sidecar/services/research/fast.py:455-498 (_news_value: the SAME 'news' tool blend IS relevance-gated via services.research.relevance.row_relevant, and drops off-entity rows with an honest _no_on_entity_news_note — explicitly built for R13 ledger #9, this exact failure class); sidecar/services/news_provider.py:63-98 (region-wide general market RSS feeds are always folded in alongside the per-symbol feed, unlabelled by entity, hence symbols: [] on the Sterling & Wilson item)
notes: R13 ledger #9 already fixed this exact bug (an off-entity namesake's feed item being read as the target company's news) for the FAST tier, but the fix was never ported to DEEP/ULTRA: deep.py's _record_structured for the news dim never calls relevance.row_relevant or filters the raw item list at all — it hands the LLM the full unfiltered blend (129 items here, most symbols: [], general market/world noise) as 'News for BDL' and the model picked an off-topic item and wrote its figures into the brief as BDL's own order book, unhedged, with a citation. This is money-relevant fabricated data presented as fact (a materially wrong order-book claim about a listed defence company), exactly the class COMMON.md rates critical. Local-lane control (11-deep-bdl-llama.jsonl, same query) did not hit this because its synthesis timed out into the honest structured floor (SURF-RESEARCH-BRIEFS-2) before any freeform prose was generated from the news blob — the bug is latent whenever DEEP/ULTRA synthesis actually completes. Smallest fix: route the DEEP/ULTRA structured news leg through the same relevance.row_relevant gate fast.py already uses (or call _news_value directly) before folding it into the researcher's prompt context, and drop off-entity items with the same honest note.

title: The 'structured data only / no web' banner can never fire: exchange and vysted:// rows count as sources, so zero-web DEEP/ULTRA briefs present as web-backed
repro: DEEP BDL and ULTRA HAL on gpt-4o-mini with web search returning 0 web sources ('0 web source(s)' step) -> replay through applyHostAction/useBriefStore: webAvailable true, noWebBanner false, degraded_reason null, sourceCount >0 (all vysted://price|fundamentals|news or exchange rows)
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/12-deep-bdl-4omini.jsonl, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/13-ultra-hal-4omini.jsonl, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/36-staleack-run2-final.jsonl ('0 web source(s)'), replay rows in docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/replay-*.json; src/lib/host-actions.ts:228 (webAvailable = sources.length > 0 || input.web_available === true)
notes: The honest 'no web — structured data only' affordance (comment :221-222 promises it survives) is dead because the auto-publish always carries structured-provenance rows. A reader cannot tell a brief whose narrative claims came from nowhere (SURF-RESEARCH-BRIEFS-10's misattribution shipped this way) from a web-grounded one. Smallest fix: count only http(s) sources (exclude vysted:// and exchange provenance) when deriving webAvailable.

title: On Ollama the auto-publish ack id is the constant '__autobrief', so one turn's panel ack silently confirms every later brief for 10 minutes
repro: same sidecar (pid 15507): turn 1 auto-publish acked applied as '__autobrief' at 08:06:03; turn 2 'research Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders' (ollama, auto) with NO ack from any client -> publish_brief '__autobrief' at 08:12:02, zero 'did not confirm the publish' notices, model says 'Built a brief on Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders.'; control on a fresh process with no prior ack (run 30) -> the notice fires (1)
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/30-staleack-run1-noack-fresh.jsonl, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/33-staleack-prior-ack-rerun.txt (verdict block), docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/36-staleack-run2-final.jsonl; sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:835,929 (id f'{tool_call_id}__autobrief' with tool_call_id '' from ollama.py:212), sidecar/services/action_ledger.py (process-global, 600 s TTL)
notes: The ledger is keyed only by the call id, and on the default local lane that id is identical for every auto-brief, so the read-back that exists to stop the model claiming an unrendered brief is defeated by any earlier success — including one from another chat or panel. Smallest fix: mint the auto-publish id from a uuid (or the research run_id) instead of the provider's tool_call_id, and consume (pop) an ack once read.

title: When the openbb-mcp child dies, /fundamentals 500s and the research SSE dies mid-stream with no done/error frame while /openbb-mcp/status still reports available
repro: openbb-mcp child on the configured port gone (process died) -> GET /openbb-mcp/status {available:true,lastError:null}; GET /fundamentals/MAZDOCK and /fundamentals/KPITTECH -> 500; research prompt on /agents/copilot/invoke cut at 63.8 s right after 'pulling market data for MAZDOCK' with no done/error frame (uvicorn: 'ASGI callable returned without completing response'; traceback: httpx.ConnectError -> CancelledError via cancel scope -> RuntimeError 'Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task'); /quotes still 200 via nse_direct. Restarting the child restores 200s
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/35-openbb-mcp-down-stream-dies.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/34-staleack-run2-rerun.jsonl; sidecar/services/mcp_client.py:102-119 (except Exception around _open does not catch the anyio CancelledError; exit_stack.aclose() runs in another task), sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:410 (fallback only catches ProviderError, so the next provider is never tried)
notes: A dead data child should be a degraded provider that falls through to the next source; instead it poisons the request task, which kills the whole agent stream — the chat and brief sit in_flight forever with no error row, and the status endpoint says all is well. Smallest fix: map transport failures (ConnectError/CancelledError from a failed MCP open) to ProviderError inside mcp_client, record lastError/available=false, and let the registry fall through.
